svg.title: Page 9, the end of chapter 1: the photograph, with Dinis's notes numbered and typed

text.tspan: Page 9, the end of chapter 1
What the pen says, word for word, and what it means
THE FIRST PAGES SELL THE BOOK
“Finally we tell the reader why they should
read this book :)”
This paragraph, the shape of the middle and 'Ship', is the
reason to read the book; it arrives on page 9.
TOPICS FIRST, DETAILS UNDER THEM
“too much detail at this stage of the book”
Build it without a server, SG/Send, sgit and RiskMandate
are too much detail for chapter 1.
MEET THE READER WHERE THEY ARE
“yes, point to our website (of this book)
where ALL materials are public → first
version of this site will have my own stand
ups :)”
The measure: point to the book's website, where all the
materials are public; the first version will carry Dinis's
own stand-ups. (Reading of 'stand ups' uncertain.)
A RELEASE, NOT A DRAFT
“new book [circled: new book that]”
The answer to 'second edition or a new book?': a new book.
A RELEASE, NOT A DRAFT
“But I really like this kind of box, but it
means we need two ... [the rest runs off the
photograph]”
The For Dinis boxes work, but they imply two versions of
the book (likely one for review and one for readers);
Dinis to confirm.
